policies.title: Serbian ordinary passport: citizen entry
policies.summary: A Serbian national travelling on an ordinary Serbian passport is classified as citizenship, not under Serbia's foreign-visitor visa regime.
conditions: This is a citizenship classification only. The cited law requires entry to be allowed when the person is established as a Serbian citizen, even without a travel document.
It does not establish foreign-passport, dual-national documentation, residence, work, transit, or final border-control treatment.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 90 days in six months, with stated identity-card route
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for up to 90 days in six months and separately state that an identity card can be used to travel to Serbia.
conditions: The policy records the ordinary-passport visitor baseline. The separate identity-card statement is not an ordinary-passport expansion and depends on the stated bilateral agreement or Government decision.
It does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
A valid document, purpose and financial proof may be required; border admission remains discretionary under the published entry requirements.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages waive visas for these ordinary passports for visits of up to 90 days in a six-month period from first entry.
conditions: This is the ordinary-passport visitor baseline only. It does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access.
A valid document, purpose and financial proof may be required; border admission remains subject to the MFA's published refusal conditions.

policies.title: Argentina ordinary passport: tourism visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA's Argentina page specifically waives a visa for tourist visits up to 90 days in a six-month period from first entry.
conditions: The published waiver is expressly for tourist visits; it does not establish work, residence, airport transit, business, diplomatic, official/service, or special-document treatment.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Moldovan biometric ordinary passport: visa-free up to 90 days in six months
policies.summary: The MFA limits Moldova's 90-day-in-six-month visa exemption to biometric passports.
conditions: Only a biometric ordinary passport is established. Non-biometric, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service and other special travel documents are not covered by this policy.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Montenegrin ordinary passport: visa-free up to 90 days
policies.summary: The MFA waives visas for Montenegrin ordinary passports for up to 90 days and separately notes a stated identity-and-citizenship document route.
conditions: The identity-and-citizenship document statement is a separate document route, not an expansion of this ordinary-passport policy.

This policy does not establish work, residence, airport transit, emergency, refugee, diplomatic, official/service, or other special-document access; final admission remains subject to published border requirements.

policies.title: Hong Kong SAR passport: visa-free up to 14 days
policies.summary: The Serbian MFA's China page waives visas for Chinese citizens holding an SAR Hong Kong passport for visits up to 14 days.
conditions: The exemption is document-specific: it applies to a Chinese citizen holding an SAR Hong Kong passport and must not be generalized to other Chinese travel documents.
The live MFA country page displays a 3 April 2018 update date, so the result is retained with medium confidence pending a newer official restatement.
Final border admission, document, purpose and financial requirements continue to apply.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: visitor visa required
policies.summary: The MFA's current country pages mark these ordinary passports as requiring a Serbian visa. The policy records the short-visitor baseline, not an electronic-visa cohort.
conditions: This is the ordinary national-passport short-visitor baseline. The short-stay C visa may cover tourism, business and other travel up to 90 days in 180; employment, education and family residence are separate long-stay D or residence matters.

Serbia has genuinely issued Digital Travel Authorizations since 23 April 2025, but the MFA only makes them available to countries enabled on the Government portal. It publishes no exhaustive current nationality mapping, so online filing or issuance is not normalized as a nationality-wide eVisa entitlement here.

A holder of a valid Schengen, UK, EU-member-state or United States visa, or a Schengen/EU/US residence permit, has a separately stated up-to-90-day document-conditioned visa-free route. That route is not inferred from passport nationality and does not alter this baseline.

Visa issuance and entry remain subject to passport validity, purpose, invitation or travel proof, funds, insurance, security, sanctions, health, transit and final border-admission requirements. This policy establishes no diplomatic, official/service, emergency, refugee or other special-document result.
